katie (cust-suc): Heads-up — customer 'Maple' opened a P1: their ingestion pipeline into Pinecone started throwing dimension errors after we rolled the embedding cache change yesterday. They see: "expected 1536 got 1024" intermittently. They say it correlates with high QPS bursts and when they switch model variants in their app. Ticket: #4521. Can we triage?

maria (support): Ack, looking. Do we know if they're using prefix-based caching in front of the embeddings endpoint (customer-side) or relying on our X-Embedding-Cache behavior? Any sample request IDs?

katie (cust-suc): They said they use our hosted embeddings endpoint with prefix reuse (they append a document id to a shared prefix). Here's a snippet they sent: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "rw-emb-small-v2", "input": "user:1234:article-9876:summary" }
```
They rotate models during experiments (some requests hit a new model with 1024 dim, others older 1536). They expected cache misses after model change but still see hits.

maria (support): Can we grab logs for the request range? Also any recent deploys to the cache logic? @deploy-bot any rollouts around that time?

deploy-bot: rollout/service/emb-cache v1.8 -> v1.9 completed at 1763467500 :rocket:

maria (support): Thanks. @jason can you pull the embedding cache access logs for customer Maple between 1763467400-1763468000? Looking for header traces like X-Embedding-Cache: hit|miss and model/dim info.

jason (eng): Pulling logs now. Found matching requests — paste of condensed log lines below (sanitized):
```
[1763467492] req=abc123 model=rw-emb-small-v1 input_prefix=user:1234:article-9876 cache=HIT cache_key=sha1(user:1234:article-9876|rw-emb-small-v1)
[1763467493] req=abc124 model=rw-emb-small-v2 input_prefix=user:1234:article-9876 cache=HIT cache_key=sha1(user:1234:article-9876|rw-emb-small-v1)
[1763467494] req=abc125 model=rw-emb-small-v2 input_prefix=user:1234:article-9876 cache=HIT cache_key=sha1(user:1234:article-9876|rw-emb-small-v1)
```
Notice model in line 2/3 is v2 (1024d) but cache_key still references v1.

alan (ml-eng): This smells like a cache key canonicalization bug. Our cache key schema was supposed to include (prefix_hash, model_name, embedding_dim, quantization_tag) but I remember a perf patch a week ago that deduped model name and dropped the explicit dims from fast path. If dims are omitted and we reuse a prefix-only key, a v2 request could return a v1 vector -> downstream dimension errors.

maria (support): So the cache reported HIT and returned a 1536 vector even though request asked for 1024? That lines up with customer errors. Any repro?

jason (eng): I reproduced locally in a stress test. Repro steps below (simplified):
1) seed cache with model v1 (1536d):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rw-emb-small-v1","input":"user:42:doc-1"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'
# response headers: X-Embedding-Cache: HIT; X-Embedding-Key: sha1(user:42:doc-1|rw-emb-small-v1)
```
2) switch model to v2 (1024d) and send same prefix at high QPS via 8 concurrent clients:
```
# many parallel requests
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rw-emb-small-v2","input":"user:42:doc-1"}' & done
wait
```
Observed: ~65% of v2 requests returned cache=HIT with vectors of length 1536. CPU profile shows race in cache metadata update: updater thread writes new model tag asynchronously, but fast-path lookup still uses old metadata if hit in same millisecond.

alan (ml-eng): Additional root cause detail: cache store is sharded; we used an atomic pointer swap for model metadata but the key derivation used a non-atomic read of the per-shard "current_model_tag" and did not include dims in the hash. Under concurrency, you can end up computing the key with old metadata while the store entry is already present for the new model (or vice versa). It's a small time-of-check/time-of-use race.

maria (support): Oof. That explains intermittent nature. What's the customer impact beyond ingestion errors? Any billing or auth implications?

jason (eng): No auth/billing anomalies observed. There is a small latency spike when cache warmups happen (miss -> hit). Customer sees their DB reject vectors with wrong dim; that translates to ingestion failures and retries — they reported higher 5xxs and queuebacks.

katie (cust-suc): Customer is pushing this to P1. They want an ETA and mitigation steps ASAP. Suggested temporary mitigation: force cache bypass for the affected workspace or set their client to versioned prefixes (append model+dim). Can we turn on a workspace-scoped 'cache_strict_mode' to include dims in key temporarily?

jason (eng): Short-term mitigation options:
- Option A (fast): Enable per-workspace strict keying in config: include explicit model_name and embedding_dim into the cache key derivation for that workspace. This is a config flip and should be low-risk.
- Option B: Roll back the perf patch that removed dims from fast-path; higher risk/time.
- Option C (customer-side): Ask Maple to append model+dim to the prefix (e.g., user:1234:model=rw-emb-small-v2:dim=1024:article-9876). Works but requires their dev effort.

maria (support): Which option is quickest to ship?

jason (eng): I can push a config flag to enable strict-keying for a workspace today; needs a deploy to the feature flag service and a quick hotfix in cache layer to read flag on lookup. Estimate 3-4 hours and a canary then rollout.

alan (ml-eng): Long-term fix: make cache key include (prefix_hash, model_name, embedding_dim, quant_tag) always and add a proper atomic swap when updating model metadata; add a unit + stress test that simulates concurrent model switches. I'll write the patch.

katie (cust-suc): Please proceed with the temporary config for Maple and communicate the workaround to them. They asked for a status update in 1h.

maria (support): Action items: @jason implement workspace-level strict-keying flag and deploy canary -> if green, enable for Maple. @alan prepare full patch and tests. @katie send customer the temporary workaround (append model+dim) and ETA ~4h. Marking P1.

jason (eng): Started branch: feat/emb-cache-strict-keying. Can confirm local tests + small canary pass for internal test workspace. Will request deploy at 1763468040.

deploy-bot: deploy/service/feature-flags v0.62 -> accepted at 1763468040

maria (support): Thanks team. I'll update ticket #4521 and let the customer know we'll enable workspace strict-keying as soon as canary finishes.

katie (cust-suc): Customer acknowledged; they will try the client-side prefix change if we need more time. :thumbsup:

alan (ml-eng): FYI I'll also add a regression test that toggles model versions under high concurrency; this should catch it before next release.

maria (support): Closing loop for now. Follow-ups: postmortem after root fix and a note in docs about prefix versioning.
